explanation: The statement says that almost every point has a nonzero middle coordinate under one specific product measure on ℝ × ℝ × ℝ: volume ⊗ (volume ⊗ volume restricted to (0,∞)). Mathlib supplies the ingredients, which the current proof already uses: measure_singleton with compl_mem_ae_iff (almost every real is nonzero under Lebesgue measure), then Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst and Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_snd to lift that fact through the product measure. Combining them takes three Mathlib facts and an intermediate step, not a single declaration with routine glue. I did not search for a ready-made 'almost every point avoids a value' lemma for Lebesgue measure. Such a lemma would only replace the first step; the two projection lifts would still be needed. No Mathlib declaration states this product-measure result directly.
